q: What are the planning levels?
a: Project plan, stage plan and team plan; an exception plan can replace an affected plan.

q: Plan versus schedule?
a: A plan also covers products, resources, control, quality and risks; a schedule focuses on timing.

q: What is a critical path?
a: A sequence of dependent activities for which delay would delay the planned completion.

q: What is an external dependency?
a: A product or event outside the project’s control that the plan needs.

q: How do you prevent scope creep?
a: Agree product descriptions and control proposed changes to their approved baselines.

q: What are the sustainability perspectives in planning?
a: Consider sustainability of delivery, the product and the long term benefits.

q: What is the first product to describe when Zosia plans SnakeBite by products?
a: Project product description. It states the overall product and acceptance criteria.

q: Zosia divides the game into a hierarchy of engine, art and audio products. Which tool is this?
a: Product breakdown structure (PBS). A PBS groups the products by part and whole.

q: Which tool shows that the engine must be completed before art integration?
a: Product flow diagram (PFD). A PFD shows product sequence and dependencies.

q: A team manager prepares an internal schedule for a work package. Which plan is this?
a: Team plan. A team plan helps the team organize its specialist work.

q: The project board requests a replacement plan after a forecast exception. Which plan does Zosia prepare?
a: Exception plan. An exception plan responds to an exception and replaces the affected plan when approved.

q: When does estimating resources and scheduling occur in product based planning?
a: After identifying products, describing them and mapping dependencies. Products and their dependencies establish the basis for estimates.

q: What is the sequence in product based planning?
a: Project product description, PBS, product descriptions, PFD. Describe the overall product before decomposing and sequencing products.

q: A hierarchical view of all products in scope is the product breakdown [...].
a: Structure (PBS). PBS stands for product breakdown structure.

q: Which TWO are PRINCE2 planning levels?
a: Project plan; Stage plan. Project and stage plans describe work at different management levels.

q: Which statement about an exception plan is FALSE?
a: It is produced automatically at the start of every stage. An exception plan is prepared in response to an exception decision.

q: A diagram showing the sequence and dependencies between products is a product flow [...].
a: Diagram (PFD). The PFD shows the order in which products are developed.

q: What should be described first in the product based planning technique?
a: The project product. The project product description establishes the overall scope and acceptance criteria.

q: Which TWO are developed while estimating and scheduling a plan?
a: Required resources; Schedule. Estimates inform the resources and timetable.

q: Which plan is normally managed without direct project board approval?
a: Team plan. The team manager uses a team plan to organize work package delivery.

q: Why does PRINCE2 use the plans practice?
a: To define products and how they will be delivered, enabling communication and control. A plan provides a shared basis for delivery and progress control.

q: What is a planning horizon?
a: The period for which a plan can be prepared with reasonable confidence. Nearer work can normally be planned in more detail.

q: When is the initiation stage plan prepared?
a: During starting up a project. Starting up produces the plan for the initiation stage.

q: Is an exception plan a fourth level in the plan hierarchy?
a: No; it is a plan used to respond to an exception. Exception plans can replace project or stage plans.
